claims: Transfuse platelets for severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count 33–63 K/uL) in a critically ill, coagulopathic patient.
Transfuse packed red blood cells for severe anemia (hemoglobin 7.1–7.9 g/dL) in a ventilated ICU patient.
Reverse coagulopathy (INR 3.6–4.1, PTT 59–67.6 sec) with vitamin K and/or fresh frozen plasma, given elevated bleeding risk.
Continue meropenem for presumed severe infection/sepsis, with cultures and source control assessment.
Continue norepinephrine infusion for hemodynamic support, titrated to mean arterial pressure goal.
Continue lung-protective mechanical ventilation (tidal volume 300 mL, PEEP 8–10 cmH2O) with daily sedation interruption assessment.
Monitor serum lactate (5.9–6.3 mmol/L) and hemodynamics to assess resuscitation response.
Monitor blood glucose (finger sticks 188–310 mg/dL) and treat hyperglycemia with insulin as needed.
Monitor electrolytes and renal function (sodium 125–127, potassium 4.8–5.2, phosphate 6.7–7.7, creatinine 3.0–3.6, BUN 69–75) and manage abnormalities.
Perform daily assessment of volume status and consider diuresis or renal replacement therapy given oliguric renal failure and hyperphosphatemia.
